messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Sev2 created: paging memory creep on inference-runtime us-west1. Symptoms: progressive RSS growth, repeated OOMKilled, CUDA driver errors. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panel=kv_paged_frag — creator: maria

maria: seeing a cluster of container restarts starting ~1748882000. Affected pool: model-pool-3 (paged-attn + KV). Logs show repeated eviction loops + some CUDA errors.

devon: looks like fragmentation is the culprit — free memory is in tiny fragments, allocs succeed then OOM on larger contiguous request. frag ratio reported ~0.78 on node-42.

jia: paste logs from node-42 of the runtime cage:
```
[2026-03-14T22:03:12Z] runtime: attempt allocate 28MB contiguous -> failed, OOM
[2026-03-14T22:03:12Z] kubernetes: container runtime: oom killed
[2026-03-14T22:03:12Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc returned CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```

kevin: any correlation with recent deploys? I see a canary for quantized-optim kernel earlier today but rolled back at 09:00. Not sure if partial rollout left weird state.

alex: immediate mitigation suggestion: 1) reduce batch size for the affected routes to limit new KV allocations, 2) lower kv eviction threshold to force more aggressive compaction, 3) temporarily disable attention paging for model-pool-3 (fallback to resident mode) to stop paged allocator churn.

maria: doing (1) now: patching config to set max_batch_tokens=800 -> rolling to frontend routers.

devon: I'll trigger a live kv-compact run on the three worst nodes (42/43/47). Command I'm running:
```bash
# trigger in-cluster compaction job
kubectl -n runtime exec -it runtime-tools -- kv-compact --nodes node-42,node-43,node-47 --mode=conservative
```

jia: kicking off compaction now. ETA ~4-6m per node, will stream logs.

customer-support: two paying customers (acme-inc, ledgerly) reported elevated 5xx rates and timeouts starting ~22:04 UTC. CS is on it, pinged customers with status "degraded".

kevin: while compaction runs, we should avoid full-scale restarts; that can spike reclaim pressure. Also propose kernel flag flip to enable slab coalescing in allocator on the nodes (hotfix via sysctl + restart of runtime daemon, not full node reboot).

devon: trying a less intrusive change first: bumping KVCACHE_EVICT_RATIO from 0.7 -> 0.6 on nodes in pool-3 config. Pushing now.

maria: applied and propagated to ~60% of nodes. Monitoring mem headrooms.

incident-bot: automation: scheduled rolling restart for pool-3 containers with pause 45s between pods to avoid thundering herd. Job id: 1748882230-roll-42.

alex: note: disabling paging will increase GPU memory usage but reduce allocator fragmentation; only flip on pools where model size fits in resident memory. We verified model-pool-3 fits with 20% headroom.

jia: compaction logs: node-42 compact pass 1 -> freed ~1.2GB fragmented pages; pass 2 -> freed 600MB; fragmentation ratio down to 0.42. No immediate OOMs since.

maria: customer-impact update: acme-inc incident created, CS posted status page: "serving degraded, some requests failing with 5xx; engineering mitigation in progress".

kevin: CUDA errors may have been secondary due to OOM-triggered driver state. Once we stabilize memory fragmentation, watch for driver error recurrences.

devon: still seeing intermittent container crash on node-47 with cgroup OOM even after compaction; investigating whether local growth pattern persists (long-tail seq_len). Adding per-pod seq_len cap 1024.

oncall-shift: handing off to night oncall @kevin in 30m. Current mitigations: compaction triggered on worst nodes, evict ratio lowered, paging disabled on pool-3, rolling restarts queued. Customer impact: degraded, two enterprise tenants affected, CS engaged. Postmortem owner: jia.

maria: thanks team. Next steps for night: monitor gpu driver metrics, watch for new OOMs, consider a gradual binpacking of high-alloc tenants to separate nodes if creep continues. Please annotate any new findings in this thread. :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll take it from here. If we see persistent fragmentation after compaction + config changes, schedule a more thorough hotfix: allocator slab coalescing + improved small-block free list. Otherwise continue with reduced batching and seq_len caps.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Sev2 status updated -> mitigations in progress; next update scheduled in 30m."
